topic: The Most Beautiful Equation: Decoding Euler's Identity (e^{iπ} = -1)
target_audience: High school students (Advanced Math) or first-year University students

sections.title: The Grand Reunion
lecture_lines: Five major mathematical constants appear from different worlds.
They converge into a single, unified cluster.
Euler’s bridge connects these fundamental numbers together.
animations: Fade in symbols 0 (#FFFFFF), 1 (#FFFF00), pi (#FF8800), e (#00FF00), and i (#00FFFF) scattered across the screen.
Move all symbols to the center to form a single, unified cluster.
Draw glowing white lines (#FFFFFF) connecting the symbols over a light gray coordinate grid (#555555).

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Nature of 'i' as a Steering Wheel
lecture_lines: Forget "imaginary"; think of i as a rotation operator.
Multiplying by i turns any vector ninety degrees left.
It's a steering wheel for the complex plane.
animations: Draw Real and Imaginary axes with '1' marked on Real.
Rotate point from (1, 0) to (0, 1) (90 degrees counter-clockwise) using [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wheel.svg].
Highlight 'i' at (0, 1) in #00FFFF with 'Rotation' label.

sections.title: Prerequisite: 'e' and the Speed of Growth
lecture_lines: Constant e represents the limit of continuous growth.
In the real world, it scales quantities exponentially.
But direction matters just as much as speed.
animations: Show 'e' in center labeled 'Base of Growth' in #00FF00.
Animate a point moving right on the axis exponentially.
Highlight 'x' in the formula e^x in #FFFF00.

sections.title: The Synthesis: Sideways Growth
lecture_lines: What happens when growth is powered by i?
Usually, growth scales a value outward along a line.
With i, growth is always perpendicular to current position.
This sideways growth creates a perfect circular orbit.
Euler’s formula describes this rotation around the origin.
animations: Draw vector from origin to (1, 0) on complex plane.
Show purple velocity vector (#FF00FF) at tip, pointing up.
Point moves in a circle; velocity vector stays tangent.
Trace a white circular path (#FFFFFF) from (1, 0).
Display formula e^{it} near the moving point.

sections.title: The Journey to π (Pi)
lecture_lines: We start our journey at one on the circle.
Define pi as the distance halfway around.
The point moves along the edge of the circle.
We track its path for exactly pi units.
Our journey ends at the negative one station.
animations: Highlight position (1, 0) on a white unit circle (#FFFFFF).
Fade in label 'Distance = pi' in orange (#FF8800) over the upper arc.
Show a red dot (#FF0000) starting its motion at (1, 0).
Animate the red dot (#FF0000) traveling exactly halfway around the circle.
Red dot arrives at (-1, 0) marked by [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/station.svg].

sections.title: The Destination: e^{iπ} = -1
lecture_lines: We start at positive one on the real line.
Traveling halfway around, we reach the exact opposite side.
Our destination is precisely at negative one.
The reunion is complete: e, i, and pi align.
Euler's identity: the most beautiful equation in math.
animations: Flash the point at (-1, 0) in bold #FF0000.
Write equation e^{i\pi} = -1 slowly in the center.
Transform equation to e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0 with pulsing effects.
Glow all constants (e, i, pi, 1, 0) in their respective colors.
Final display: 'The Most Beautiful Equation' appears in #FFD700, marked by [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/landmark.svg] to signify its mathematical importance.
